commits.pr_title: [Bugfix] Accept RFC 2397 parameters in base64 data URLs
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

Data URLs with RFC 2397 parameters between the mediatype and the base64 marker (e.g. `data:image/jpeg;charset=utf-8;base64,...`) are rejected with an opaque HTTP 501 ("Only base64 data URLs are supported for now"), because `MediaConnector._load_data_url` splits the header on the *first* `;` and requires the remainder to equal `base64`. RFC 2397 explicitly allows such parameters, and clients that emit them (e.g. a charset param) cannot send multimodal content at all.

Changes in `vllm/multimodal/media/connector.py`:
- Take the last `;`-separated token of the header as the encoding marker (case-insensitive, and only when a real `;` precedes it, per the RFC grammar `data:[<mediatype>][;base64],<data>`), so any number of intermediate parameters is accepted.
- Strip parameters from the mediatype before passing it to `MediaIO.load_base64` — `VideoMediaIO` compares it against `video/jpeg`, so parameters must not leak through.
- Raise `ValueError` (→ HTTP 400) with a clear message when the `,` separator is missing, instead of the previous tuple-unpacking error.

Behavior preserved: non-base64 data URLs (percent-encoded per RFC 2397) still raise `NotImplementedError` (→ 501), including `data:base64,<data>` where `base64` sits in the (bogus) mediatype position.

Not a duplicate: searched open/closed issues and PRs for the exact error message, "RFC 2397", "data URI", `_load_data_url`, and related keywords — no existing work addresses this. For comparison, vLLM's own batch path (`run_batch.py`) already parses data URLs leniently (checks `"base64" in header`), and sglang's loaders accept these URLs as well (they split on the first comma and discard the header entirely) — only this interactive serving path is strict.

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used for this change; every line has been reviewed by the submitter.

## Test Plan

```
pytest tests/multimodal/media/test_connector.py -k "base64 or data_url or error_conversion"
```

New tests: `test_fetch_image_data_url_with_params` (parameters between mediatype and `;base64` load correctly, sync + async) and `test_fetch_image_data_url_malformed` (missing `,` → `ValueError`; percent-encoded and `data:base64,...` → `NotImplementedError`).

## Test Result

`31 passed` (3 new + 28 pre-existing base64 round-trip tests), macOS CPU build. `pre-commit run` (ruff, mypy, etc.) passes on the diff. Input parsing only — no model-output-affecting changes, so no eval run.

commits.pr_title: [UX] Improve data-parallel launch validation
commits.pr_body:
# [UX] Raise actionable errors for invalid data-parallel launch options

## Purpose

Replacing data-parallel launch combination assertions with plain `ValueError` at their existing validation stages, using a consistent prefix, the relevant CLI flags and values, and a corrective action. It also validates the lower bound of `--node-rank` before constructing `ParallelConfig`.

This does not duplicate [#45150](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/45150): that PR detects implicit multi-node placement when the Ray distributed executor is combined with the MP data-parallel backend, while this change improves the existing `EngineArgs` validation of explicit launch-option combinations.

## Reproducer

```python
import os

os.environ["VLLM_LOGGING_LEVEL"] = "ERROR"

from vllm import EngineArgs


MODEL = "deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V2-Lite-Chat"

CASES = {
    "hybrid_and_external": {
        "data_parallel_size": 2,
        "data_parallel_size_local": 2,
        "data_parallel_hybrid_lb": True,
        "data_parallel_external_lb": True,
    },
    "hybrid_without_local_size": {
        "data_parallel_size": 2,
        "data_parallel_hybrid_lb": True,
    },
    "multinode_without_mp": {
        "nnodes": 2,
        "data_parallel_backend": "ray",
    },
    "world_size_not_divisible": {
        "nnodes": 2,
        "data_parallel_backend": "mp",
    },
    "node_rank_out_of_bounds": {
        "nnodes": 2,
        "node_rank": 2,
        "data_parallel_backend": "mp",
        "tensor_parallel_size": 2,
    },
    "external_without_rank": {
        "data_parallel_size": 2,
        "data_parallel_external_lb": True,
    },
    "external_rank_with_local_size": {
        "data_parallel_size": 2,
        "data_parallel_rank": 0,
        "data_parallel_size_local": 2,
    },
}


def main() -> None:
    for name, kwargs in CASES.items():
        try:
            EngineArgs(model=MODEL, **kwargs).create_engine_config()
        except Exception as exc:
            print(f"{name}: {type(exc).__name__}: {exc}")
        else:
            print(f"{name}: no error")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
```

```bash
.venv/bin/python repro.py
```

The reproducer loads model configuration only; it does not load model weights.

## Output on main

```text
hybrid_and_external: AssertionError: data_parallel_hybrid_lb and data_parallel_external_lb cannot both be True.
hybrid_without_local_size: AssertionError: data_parallel_size_local must be set to use data_parallel_hybrid_lb.
multinode_without_mp: AssertionError: nnodes > 1 is only supported with data_parallel_backend=mp
world_size_not_divisible: AssertionError: world_size=1 must be divisible by nnodes=2.
node_rank_out_of_bounds: AssertionError: node_rank=2 must be less than nnodes=2.
external_without_rank: AssertionError: data_parallel_rank or node_rank must be specified if data_parallel_external_lb is enable.
external_rank_with_local_size: AssertionError: data_parallel_size_local must be 1 or None when data_parallel_rank is set
```

## Output on this branch

```text
hybrid_and_external: ValueError: Invalid data-parallel launch options: `--data-parallel-hybrid-lb` and `--data-parallel-external-lb` cannot be enabled together. Enable only one load-balancing mode.
hybrid_without_local_size: ValueError: Invalid data-parallel launch options: `--data-parallel-hybrid-lb` requires `--data-parallel-size-local`. Set it to the number of data-parallel ranks on this node.
multinode_without_mp: ValueError: Invalid data-parallel launch options: `--nnodes 2` requires `--data-parallel-backend mp`; got `--data-parallel-backend ray`. Use the MP backend or set `--nnodes 1`.
world_size_not_divisible: ValueError: Invalid data-parallel launch options: `--nnodes 2` must evenly divide the total world size (1). Adjust `--nnodes`, `--data-parallel-size`, `--pipeline-parallel-size`, or `--tensor-parallel-size`.
node_rank_out_of_bounds: ValueError: Invalid data-parallel launch options: `--node-rank` must be between 0 and 1; got `--node-rank 2`. Set it to this node's zero-based index.
external_without_rank: ValueError: Invalid data-parallel launch options: `--data-parallel-external-lb` requires a data-parallel rank. Set `--data-parallel-rank`, or set `--data-parallel-size` greater than 1 and use `--nnodes` with `--node-rank` so the rank can be inferred.
external_rank_with_local_size: ValueError: Invalid data-parallel launch options: an external data-parallel rank requires `--data-parallel-size-local 1`; got 2. Set it to 1 or omit it.
```

The same branch output was also verified under `.venv/bin/python -O`.

## Test Plan

```bash
HF_HUB_CACHE=/data/engine/hub_cache HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 \
  .venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/engine/test_arg_utils.py::test_invalid_data_parallel_launch_options \
  tests/engine/test_arg_utils.py::test_valid_multinode_data_parallel_launch_options \
  -x -q

PRE_COMMIT_HOME=/tmp/pre-commit .venv/bin/pre-commit run \
  --files vllm/engine/arg_utils.py tests/engine/test_arg_utils.py
```

Result: 9 cases passed in 1.72 seconds; all applicable pre-commit hooks passed. The complete 105-test module also passed on an NVIDIA B300 (85-test and 20-test shards).

No new CI cost: this extends an existing CPU test module with focused validation tests and adds no fixtures, dependencies, or CI jobs. Model evaluation is not applicable because this changes configuration validation only and cannot affect model output.

## AI assistance

OpenAI Codex (GPT-5) assisted with drafting the code, regression test, and PR description. I reviewed every changed line, and I ran the commands reported above.

commits.pr_title: [UX] Reject incompatible nested runtime overrides
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

Runtime configuration overrides validated nested values only by checking whether they were any dataclass, so an unrelated dataclass could silently replace the expected nested config type. Other invalid overrides used assertions that disappeared under `python -O`, producing low-level attribute errors instead. This change accepts only mappings or instances of the expected nested dataclass, reports the complete nested field path through one recursive validation helper.  Unsupported runner configs and unknown fields now raise contextual `ValueError`s.

## Reproducer

Run with `VLLM_LOGGING_LEVEL=ERROR .venv/bin/python -O repro.py`:

```python
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from typing import Any

from vllm.config.utils import update_config


@dataclass
class Inner:
    value: int = 1


@dataclass
class Outer:
    inner: Inner = field(default_factory=Inner)


@dataclass
class Other:
    value: str = "bad"


def run_case(name: str, overrides: dict[str, Any]) -> None:
    try:
        updated = update_config(Outer(), overrides)
    except Exception as exc:
        print(f"{name}: {type(exc).__name__}: {exc}")
    else:
        print(f"{name}: accepted inner_type={type(updated.inner).__name__}")


def main() -> None:
    run_case("wrong_dataclass", {"inner": Other()})
    run_case("wrong_nested_type", {"inner": "bad"})
    run_case("unknown_nested_field", {"inner": {"missing": 1}})


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
```

## Output on main

```text
wrong_dataclass: accepted inner_type=Other
wrong_nested_type: AttributeError: 'str' object has no attribute 'items'
unknown_nested_field: AttributeError: 'Inner' object has no attribute 'missing'
```

## Output on this branch

```text
wrong_dataclass: ValueError: Override for Outer.inner must be a mapping or Inner, got Other
wrong_nested_type: ValueError: Override for Outer.inner must be a mapping or Inner, got str
unknown_nested_field: ValueError: Outer.inner.missing is not a valid config field
```

## AI assistance

OpenAI Codex (GPT-5) assisted with drafting the code, tests, and PR description. I reviewed every changed line and personally ran the commands reported above.

commits.pr_title: Encoder cache extension hooks
commits.pr_body: ## Purpose This PR adds extension hooks for the V1 encoder cache lifecycle so downstream or out-of-tree implementations can customize encoder cache behavior without changing the default vLLM path. Concretely, this PR: - Adds `EncoderCacheManagerConfig` and `EncoderCacheManagerMetadata`. - Allows `VllmConfig` to provide a custom scheduler-side encoder cache manager class via `ec_manager_config.encoder_cache_manager_cls`. - Propagates encoder cache manager metadata through `SchedulerOutput`. - Adds overridable `GPUModelRunner` hooks for request cleanup, scheduler encoder-cache updates, encoder output caching, and encoder output lookup. - Preserves the existing default behavior: the built-in encoder cache manager returns no metadata, and the default runner hooks continue to use the existing `encoder_cache` dictionary and EC connector save/free flow. This is intended to make custom encoder cache managers easier to integrate while keeping the upstream default path behavior-preserving. This PR was motivated by the Ascend score-based encoder cache implementation. That implementation uses a two-level cache: - A small and fast NPU cache for hot encoder outputs. - A larger CPU cache for less frequently accessed encoder outputs. - A score-based promotion and eviction policy that considers access frequency, aging, and estimated encoder recomputation cost. The scheduler decides whether an encoder output: 1. Is already available in the NPU cache. 2. Is available in CPU cache and should be temporarily staged to NPU. 3. Should be promoted from CPU cache to the persistent NPU cache. 4. Should be evicted or freed from one of the cache levels. 5. Must be recomputed because it is not present in either level. Before this PR, the scheduler could not pass these decisions to the model runner, and platform implementations had to override or copy large parts of `Scheduler` and `GPUModelRunner`. Such copies are difficult to maintain and can easily diverge from upstream vLLM. This PR adds the minimum lifecycle hooks and metadata channel required by this use case. The Ascend score-cache implementation itself remains in vllm-ascend and is not included in this PR. ## Test Plan - Recommended before merge: - `.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_model_runner_mm_gather.py -q` - If validating a concrete custom manager, run an integration test that sets `ec_manager_config.encoder_cache_manager_cls` and verifies metadata propagation from scheduler output to the model runner. ## Test Result - This PR has passed the basic vLLM test suite, confirming its compatibility with the existing default path. - The performance evaluation results on Ascend are shown below. We evaluated the implementation across multiple public datasets. ## Contributions - `hanxi` @hanxi-java proposed the vLLM plugin-oriented extension approach. - `zhukexin` @hotTea123 and `hanxi` co-developed the vLLM plugin-oriented design. - The hook design was motivated and validated by a downstream Ascend score encoder cache use case. This use case was jointly proposed, developed, and tested by `zhukexin` and `wangqing` @sereinnwang; special thanks to `chenminghao` @HMCCMH for the support in design communication and testing validation. The Ascend implementation is not included in this PR.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix] Skip linear bias in layerwise reload to avoid corruption
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

Linear layers that carry a `bias` are corrupted when loaded through the online quantization + layerwise-reload path (e.g. online FP8). After loading, `bias` holds uninitialized memory instead of the checkpoint values.

**Root cause.** The linear base class creates `bias` *after* `create_weights()`. Online quantization calls `initialize_online_processing()` from inside `create_weights()`, i.e. before `bias` exists, so:

1. `load_numel_total = get_layer_size(layer)` counts only `weight`, and
2. `bias`'s weight loader is never wrapped into `online_process_loader`, so it is never buffered into `info.loaded_weights`.

As soon as `weight` finishes loading, `load_numel >= load_numel_total` holds and `_layerwise_process()` runs. `materialize_layer()` re-allocates every non-skipped tensor of the layer via `empty_strided` — including the already-loaded, non-meta `bias` — replacing its real values with uninitialized memory. Since `bias` is absent from `loaded_weights`, the replay loop never writes it back, so the corruption is permanent.

**Fix.** Add `"bias"` to `SKIP_TENSORS`. `bias` is never quantized (FP8 only quantizes `weight`; `bias` stays bf16 and is added after the GEMM), it is tiny, and it is eager-loaded on the normal path, so it should never be moved to meta or re-materialized by the layerwise-reload path.

## Test Plan

Load a model with biased linear layers (Qwen3 vision tower `visual.blocks.*` qkv/proj/mlp) using online FP8 quantization + layerwise reload, then compare every `bias` parameter against the original bf16 checkpoint with `torch.allclose`.

## Test Result

- **Before:** all 110 vision-tower biases mismatch the checkpoint (`allclose` fails; values are uninitialized/zero).
- **After:** all 110 biases match the checkpoint exactly (`allclose` passes).

Tracing on `visual.blocks.0.attn.proj` confirms the mechanism: `load_numel_total=1327104` (weight only) while the recomputed layer size at trigger time is `1328256` — the 1152-element difference is exactly the bias (hidden dim). Before the fix the bias pointer changes and `absmax` drops from 3.578 to 0 across `materialize_layer()`; after the fix the pointer is unchanged and the values are preserved.

---

<summary> Essential Elements of an Effective PR Description Checklist </summary>

- [x] The purpose of the PR, such as "Fix some issue (link existing issues this PR will resolve)".
- [x] The test plan, such as providing test command.
- [x] The test results, such as pasting the results comparison before and after, or e2e results
- [ ] (Optional) The necessary documentation update, such as updating `supported_models.md` and `examples` for a new model.

commits.pr_title: [PD][NixlPush][Bugfix] Fix blocking handshake call on writer thread
commits.pr_body:
Address S2 here https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/48633.

P->D Handshakes on Push mode are initiated by the writer thread and they are currently **blocking** (that's not the case for D->P ones which are correctly async with `_send_registration_to_p`).
This is an issue under load when one or more new D instances are being spun up (eg as a result of auto-scaling), leading to noticeable performance degradation as handshakes usually take a few seconds, and the rest of the requests may remain stuck waiting to be pushed to D.

This PR re-uses the same approach we've been using with Pull mode and D->P handshakes, that is offloading the handshake to the background thread (already present in base_worker.py) as async task.

## Test with

`pytest -v -s tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_push_connector.py`

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix] Fix humming kernel crash when layer.has_bias is None
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose ##
* Fix HYV3 model with CT inference

## Testing ##
* Validated that `RedHatAI/Hy3-NVFP4-FP8` runs

## RCA
- `LinearBase.__init__` sets `self.has_bias = bias`, and some custom model layers (e.g. `Hy3-NVFP4-FP8`) pass `bias=None`. This `None` propagates as `has_bias=None` into `HummingLayerMeta`.
- `BaseHummingConfig.to_cpp_str()` skips any field whose value fails `isinstance(value, (bool, int, Enum))` — `None` fails this check, so `kHasBias` is omitted from the generated C++ struct.
- NVRTC then fails with: `class "LayerConfig" has no member "kHasBias"`.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix] Detect mixed precision in packed KV cache specs
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

Fix KV-cache zeroer initialization when mixed-precision attention specs are
packed in `UniformTypeKVCacheSpecs`.

The worker-side `KVCacheConfig.has_mixed_precision_kv_cache` check only
inspected top-level `AttentionSpec` objects. Packed specs were skipped, while
`generate_scheduler_kv_cache_config` unpacked them. This let the scheduler mark
blocks for zeroing without the worker creating a zeroer, causing the first
request to fail.

This change inspects the inner attention specs and adds a regression test that
checks worker and scheduler configurations agree.

Duplicate-work check: I searched open vLLM PRs for `#47574`, `wrapped KV cache
zeroing`, and `UniformTypeKVCacheSpecs mixed precision`; no PR addressing this
fix was found.

## Test Plan

- Run the focused regression test.
- Run the complete nearby KV-cache utility test file.
- Run pre-commit on both changed files.
- Serve the official `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-DSpark` checkpoint with
  DSpark, FP8 KV cache, and TP=2, then submit a completion request.

## Test Result

- Before the fix, the regression test failed because
  `worker_config.needs_kv_cache_zeroing` was false.
- After the fix:

commits.pr_title: [Docs] Fix broken anchor links in serving/pooling/MoE docs
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

Four in-page anchors in the docs point at fragments that do not exist on the rendered site, so the links land at the top of the target page instead of the intended section.

| Link | Problem | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `scoring.md#rerank-api` (4x) | heading is `### Cohere Rerank API` | `#cohere-rerank-api` |
| `moe_kernel_features.md#fused-moe-experts-kernels` | heading is `## Fused Experts Kernels` | `#fused-experts-kernels` |
| `openai_compatible_server.md#chat-template` | the `## Chat Template` section is in `serving/online_serving/README.md`, not in `openai_compatible_server.md` | same-page `#chat-template` |
| `generative_scoring.md#generative-scoring-api` | no such heading in that page | link to the page |

## Test Plan

- Compared every relative `#fragment` link under `docs/` against the anchors actually emitted on <https://docs.vllm.ai> (e.g. `cohere-rerank-api`, `fused-experts-kernels`, `chat-template` on the Online Serving page).
- `markdownlint-cli2` (the version pinned in `.pre-commit-config.yaml`) passes on all four changed files.

## Test Result

`Summary: 0 error(s)` from markdownlint on the changed files; all four replacement anchors exist on the published pages.

## Note

The scan also surfaced a separate class of mismatch: anchors such as `docs/design/fusions.md#allreduce--rmsnorm-fuse_allreduce_rms` are valid for GitHub's slugifier (which markdownlint's MD051 checks against) but not for the site, because `mkdocs.yaml` leaves `toc` on Python-Markdown's default slugify, which collapses repeated separators. Fixing those in the Markdown source would make MD051 fail, so it likely wants a `toc: slugify:` config change instead. Left out of this PR — happy to open a follow-up issue if that's useful.

commits.pr_title: [BugFix][LoRA] Skip marlin-backend gpt-oss LoRA tests on XPU
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose ## 
Fix XPU crashes in test_gpt_oss_lora_tp2 and test_gpt_oss_lora when mxfp4_use_marlin=True due to an unsupported MXFP4 Marlin backend.

##  Root cause ## 
The tests explicitly request moe_backend="marlin" and linear_backend="marlin", but Marlin MXFP4 kernels are CUDA‑only and not registered for XPU. Explicit requests fail instead of falling back, unlike the auto path which correctly skips Marlin on XPU.

##  Fix ## 
The ROCm skipif already exists for this reason; this PR adds the equivalent XPU condition to skip the tests as well.
